environment.description: Same application deployed behind AWS AppSync with a pipeline resolver configuration. The AppSync endpoint has request mapping templates that perform VTL-based input validation before forwarding to the Lambda-backed data source. Specifically, the updateUser mutation's request mapping template includes a conditional check: #if($ctx.args.input.profile && !$ctx.args.input.profile.settings) that short-circuits with $util.error() when profile is provided without the full nested structure. Additionally, an AWS WAF WebACL is attached to the AppSync API with a custom rule group containing a rate-based rule (100 req/5min per IP) and a regex pattern set matching against the request body. However, the WAF rule uses a SizeConstraint on body (max 8KB) and a regex pattern that flags requests containing both 'updateUser' and 'settings' keywords when the body size exceeds 2KB — this is a secondary heuristic control. The primary gate is the AppSync VTL request mapping template which validates that for user ID '2' (or any user where the backing DynamoDB item has 'profile' as NULL), mutations targeting profile.settings are rejected with a 400 before reaching the resolver Lambda.

config.request_validation: VTL request mapping template with null-safety checks on nested input fields
config.vtl_template_logic: #if($ctx.args.id == '2' && $ctx.args.input.profile.settings) $util.error('Cannot update settings for user with null profile', 'ValidationError') #end
config.dynamodb_check: Condition expression on PutItem ensures profile != NULL when settings update attempted
